faq.title: Frequently asked questions.
faq.intro: What to know about timestamp editing, compatibility, and installation.

items.question: What is File Date Editor?
items.answer: It is a desktop utility that reads and edits file creation, modification, and last-access timestamps where the operating system and file system permit it. The verified native app runs on macOS 14 or later.

items.question: Does it modify file contents?
items.answer: Timestamp edits update file system attributes. The app leaves the file contents intact. The operating system may independently update its own metadata change time.

items.question: Is an internet connection required?
items.answer: The macOS app works offline for locally available files. You need a connection to download a release or to make a cloud-only file available locally.

items.question: Can I change multiple files at once?
items.answer: Yes. On macOS, you can apply dates to the selected files or the whole list. Review each file’s result because some files or dates may be restricted.

items.question: Can I restore original dates?
items.answer: The Files tab restores the snapshot captured when a file was added to the current session. If history was enabled, a history entry can restore an earlier change when the original file is still identifiable and writable.

items.question: Does it work with PDF and Word documents?
items.answer: Yes, locally available PDF and Word documents can be treated as ordinary files, subject to file permissions and volume support. The app edits their file system dates and leaves information inside the document intact.

items.question: What is the difference between file dates and internal document metadata?
items.answer: The file system records dates for a file as a whole. A PDF or Word document may also contain its own creation date, author, and other metadata inside the document. Those values are separate.

items.question: Does the application require administrator permissions?
items.answer: On macOS the app requests access through the file picker or Finder drag and drop. Routine edits to writable files use your current permissions. Protected or read-only files may be unavailable for editing.

items.question: Why are some timestamps unavailable?
items.answer: File systems vary in which timestamps they support, their precision and date range. File permissions, read-only media, and cloud placeholders can also limit edits. The app shows restrictions and reports the values read back after writing.

items.question: Why does Windows SmartScreen show a warning?
items.answer: SmartScreen checks the reputation of downloaded files. A new or unfamiliar installer may trigger a warning. Use the official release page, check the publisher and published SHA-256, and stop if you cannot verify the download.

items.question: Why does macOS Gatekeeper show a warning?
items.answer: Gatekeeper checks the developer signature and notarization status of downloaded apps. Use a signed, notarized release from the project. If macOS reports a security problem or you cannot verify the source, do not run the build.

items.question: How do I uninstall the application?
items.answer: On macOS, quit the app and move it from Applications to the Trash. Clear change history in the app first if you want to remove stored entries. For a published Windows installer, follow its release instructions or use Installed apps. For a portable ZIP, remove the extracted files.

sections.title: Files and timestamps
sections.description: The macOS app accesses files you select in the system file picker or drop from Finder. It reads and writes system dates locally. The macOS app has no file upload or account feature.

sections.title: Local settings and change history
sections.description: Preferences are kept on your Mac using macOS UserDefaults. If history is enabled, the app stores paths, operation times, original, requested and verified dates, results, file identifiers, and security-scoped bookmarks in History.json within the app’s local Application Support directory. Clear history in the app to remove those records and bookmarks.

sections.title: Website and interactive demo
sections.description: The demonstration uses a synthetic file and keeps its values in browser memory. The website has no analytics or advertising integration. Your theme preference is stored in your browser. The hosting provider may process standard request information to deliver the site.

sections.title: Downloads and updates
sections.description: This site obtains public release information from GitHub when a repository is configured. Downloads open on GitHub, where GitHub’s own privacy policy applies. Check the Downloads page for updates.

sections.title: Timestamp editing
